title: Reject a bad ledger file quickly, and say why

blocks.text: The bank's ledger files arrive at night: a few million rows, one amount per row, and the import totals them on a `ForkJoinPool`. When a file has a bad row the whole file is rejected and someone fixes it by hand in the morning. The scheduler creates one `LedgerImport` at startup and uses it for every file of the night. Two complaints from the people who fix the files:

items: the rejection in the log reads `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: row 88412: not an amount: 1.204,00`, and the ticketing system, which expects `row 88412: not an amount: 1.204,00`, files it under "unknown";
after a rejection, the import keeps all the CPUs busy for as long as a good file takes.

blocks.text: Finish `original` and `compute()` of the `Total` task in `src/main/java/practice/LedgerImport.java`. When you're done:

items: a good file is totalled, and a file with a bad row ends `total` with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message is exactly `"row " + index + ": "` and the parser's message;
once a row has turned out bad, the rest of the file is left mostly unparsed;
a rejected file doesn't change what the next file on the same `LedgerImport` returns.

blocks.text: About fifteen lines in total. The tests run real pools of two and three workers.

cases.says: good files of any size are totalled at any threshold, and a file with a bad row ends total with an IllegalArgumentException
the IllegalArgumentException the caller gets has exactly the message the failing task gave it, not the message of a copy made on another thread
once a row has failed, the other tasks stop parsing, instead of running the rest of the file to the end
a rejected file leaves nothing behind that stops the next file on the same LedgerImport from being totalled

origin.section: A Subtask's Exception Reaches join() as a Copy, and Its Siblings Keep Running

concepts: A subtask's exception reaches a joining thread on another thread as a new exception of the same class with the original as its cause, one copy per thread crossed, so its message can be null or prefixed; the original is found by following getCause() while it is the same class.
A failure doesn't stop the other subtasks: forked halves that were never joined still run, so tasks that should stop after a failure check a flag that the failing task sets.
